messages:
Maya (CS): quick note — PolarisHealth onboarding: observed a ~30% jump in token cost this week and tail latency spikes on long discharge summaries. Renewal check in ~6 weeks, want to reduce cost and stabilize tail while keeping accuracy for SOAP notes. Suggestion: int8 quant + route 80% traffic to compact model for templates, keep full model for high-importance prompts.
Sam (Solutions): can you drop example traces and a typical prompt distribution? also any evals where accuracy shifted after quant?
Maya (CS): adding snippets below. 80/20 traffic split sounds reasonable as a canary. traces: "latency_tail_p95: 1.9s -> 3.4s" on >1024 tokens. token mix: 60% short (<=128), 30% medium (129-1024), 10% long (>1024).
Jordan (Polaris): we did notice cost spike after adding auto-summarize. hallucination risk is our main worry for discharge conclusions. can compact model keep clinical fidelity?
Nikhil (Eng-ML): compact variants keep most factuality for templated outputs; concerns are for freeform diagnostic text. propose hybrid strategy: prefix-based routing + int8 quant on compact. route when prompt matches templates or contains metadata flags. fallback to full model on uncertainty.
Miguel (SRE): ops note — prefix routing + KV cache will also reduce token churn for repeat templates. need to ensure cache TTL respects PHI retention rules.
Sam (Solutions): here's a quick canary config we can try (low-risk):
```json
{
  "canary": {
    "traffic_split": {"compact-v1": 0.2, "full-v2": 0.8},
    "quant_profile": "int8-safe",
    "routing_rules": [
      {"match": "template:.*(discharge|summary|medlist)", "route": "compact-v1"},
      {"match": "intent:high_criticality", "route": "full-v2"}
    ]
  }
}
```
Maya (CS): I'll request a formal enablement session with Polaris to tag templates and train their client to send the template flag. Jordan, can your devs add a header like `X-Polaris-Template: discharge_v2`?
Jordan (Polaris): yes, we can add that header for server-side requests. timeline: 2 sprint days.
Nikhil (Eng-ML): also recommend running a small eval set (50 golden discharge notes) to compare ROUGE/EM and a few clinical QA checks between full-v2 and int8 compact. I'll prepare eval harness.
Maya (CS): capture this as an action item for renewal deck — cost delta + quality regression checks.
Miguel (SRE): deploy-bot, can we do a staged canary with shadowing enabled for 48h then 5% traffic for 6 hours, monitor p95/p99 and error rate?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: shadowing=48h -> rollout 5% for 6h -> review. links: https://console.redwood.internal/canaries/7192468100
Jordan (Polaris): one more ask — can we opt-out specific endpoints that are audited? some discharge endpoints go to compliance review.
Sam (Solutions): yes — routing rules can list endpoint exceptions. I'll add an exclude list.
Maya (CS): thanks team — I'll sync with Polaris on the header work and send a calendar invite for the eval session. tagging renewal team for visibility. :thumbsup:
Jordan (Polaris): thanks all, appreciate the low-risk plan. we want clear rollback criteria (quality drop >2% or p99 >4s).
Nikhil (Eng-ML): acknowledged — will set alerting thresholds and automated rollback if criteria met.
Maya (CS): closing loop — action items: 1) Polaris dev adds header (Jordan) 2) Nikhil prepares eval harness 3) Sam drafts canary exclude list 4) Miguel schedules canary with ops 5) Maya puts summary in renewal deck.
Jordan (Polaris): confirmed.
Maya (CS): will report back after 72h of shadowing.
